parameters.content:
## Client Intake Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: An email to the intake address, a website form submission, or a phone note typed into the shared inbox starts intake for that enquiry.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Nothing is sent to an enquirer except the acknowledgement until a person approves; no advice or fee is ever quoted automatically.
   - Conflict results are shown with their evidence; a hit blocks the engagement letter until a person clears it.
   - Enquiry content is processed through an API with no data retention and stored only in the firm's own systems.
   - Out-of-scope or conflicted matters get a courteous decline drafted for approval, never an automatic one.
   - Every intake keeps an audit line: received, classified, checked, approved by whom, when.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/client-intake-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $247/month · custom $3,500–6,000 one-time

nodes.name: Gmail Trigger: Receive the enquiry
nodes.notes:
Receive the enquiry

Email body and attachments, form fields, or the phone note; sender details and the time received.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Intake inbox and web form
- Matter system (Clio, PracticePanther, a spreadsheet)
- Client, former-client and adverse-party lists
- Engagement letter templates and fee schedule
- Firm matter taxonomy

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Classify the matter" step of the Client Intake Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Matter type from the firm's own taxonomy (employment, commercial, family, conveyancing…), urgency, and whether it is within the firm's practice at all.

Rules:
- Nothing is sent to an enquirer except the acknowledgement until a person approves; no advice or fee is ever quoted automatically.
- Conflict results are shown with their evidence; a hit blocks the engagement letter until a person clears it.
- Enquiry content is processed through an API with no data retention and stored only in the firm's own systems.
- Out-of-scope or conflicted matters get a courteous decline drafted for approval, never an automatic one.
- Every intake keeps an audit line: received, classified, checked, approved by whom, when.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

Approve

The responsible person sees the classification, the conflict result, the extracted facts and the draft; approve, edit, reassign or decline.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Rejected: Approve
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.
